text:
maria: Hey team, just triaging a customer escalation. Python SDK streaming generator stops yielding after ~12s when customer hits token rotation and billing metadata header is missing. They see intermittent 204 responses from our API and the client generator never resumes. Repro attached below.

aj: ugh, do we have logs from the customer request id?

maria: customer provided request-id: rq_01G7X2Z8. Logs show server returning chunked SSE, then a 204 with Content-Length:0 right after token refresh. snippet: `...
data: {"delta":"hello"}


HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Content-Length: 0

`

nate: is this the classic auth header being nulled during rotation? iirc older py-sdk had a bug where headers were rebuilt without auth until refresh finished.

devex: what sdk version? customers often run pinned older versions.

customer-ops: they're on redwood-sdk==0.9.3 and python 3.9.7.

aj: ok that's pre-1.0.0. 0.9.x had a retry/backoff difference too. can you paste minimal repro?

maria: minimal repro (sanitized):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="...", sdk_version="0.9.3")

def stream():
    resp = client.responses.stream(model="rwd-1.0", input="hello")
    for chunk in resp:
        print(chunk)

stream()
```

maria: customer says output prints a couple tokens then hangs forever until they kill process.

devex: did they set any stream_timeout or read timeout?

customer-ops: no, default configs. also noticed they had billing-metadata header plugin that sometimes strips headers when refreshing billing token.

sre-jen: attaching runtime trace from logs:

```
2026-02-12T18:41:02Z INFO chunk: {"delta":"He"}
2026-02-12T18:41:03Z INFO chunk: {"delta":"llo"}
2026-02-12T18:41:04Z INFO token-refresh: start
2026-02-12T18:41:04Z WARN outgoing-headers: auth header temporarily empty
2026-02-12T18:41:04Z INFO HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
2026-02-12T18:41:04Z ERROR client: generator waiting on buffer, no delimiter
```

aj: so server sent 204 (no content) while the client was mid-stream. Our SSE parser expects either `\n\n` delim or `data:` lines; a bare 204 could make the client think stream terminated cleanly, but the generator is still waiting because our iterator only stops on EOF, and some older code path forgot to set EOF on 204.

devex: iirc we had a fix that converts 204->EOF for chunked SSE in 1.0.0. Confirm?

nate: yes patch #1042. 0.9.3 would leave the underlying socket open if Content-Length:0 and not signal generator to raise StopAsyncIteration.

maria: customer can't upgrade right away, need a workaround. Any ideas?

aj: short-term workaround: wrap the stream iterator with a timer and if no new chunk after X secs, close iterator and re-open with `resume=true` or re-request. Ugly but quick.

devex: snippet for workaround:

```python
import time
from contextlib import suppress

def guarded_stream(resp, idle_timeout=5):
    last = time.time()
    it = iter(resp)
    while True:
        try:
            chunk = next(it)
            last = time.time()
            yield chunk
        except StopIteration:
            return
        except Exception as e:
            # network hiccup, break and let caller retry
            raise
        if time.time() - last > idle_timeout:
            # assume hung on 204/state-flush; force reconnect
            break

# usage: for c in guarded_stream(client.responses.stream(...)):
#            print(c)
```

customer-ops: forwarded workaround to customer. They asked if this is a bug on our side.

maria: yes this is a bug in 0.9.x SDK. Root cause: race between auth token rotation and streaming SSE handling. When token refresh clears headers and server responds with 204 (internal), client SSE parser can end up buffered without emitting EOF.

aj: action items:
- devex: publish KB article with workaround + recommended upgrade path (owner: devex)
- eng-runtime: backport 1.0.0 patch that converts 204->EOF for streaming responses to 0.9.x branch if feasible (owner: nate)
- support-bot: add temporary alert to watch for increased rate of `generator waiting on buffer` errors (owner: support-bot)

devex: I'll draft KB and quick pip upgrade instructions. Also note to customers: `pip install --upgrade redwood-sdk>=1.0.0` fixes this properly.

nate: I'll evaluate backport complexity. if not, we can ship hotfix 0.9.4 with small patch to force EOF on Content-Length:0 for chunked streams.

support-bot: created ticket INF-5213 and added slack alert to #support for `generator waiting on buffer` >= 3/min :rotating_light:.

customer-ops: customer confirmed workaround works for them (idle_timeout=6). thanks.

maria: nice, please keep me posted on backport. Also add a note to release notes about streaming auth races.

sre-jen: one more note: if customers add custom header middleware for billing tokens, remind them to not drop `Authorization` during refresh; provide example middleware to swap tokens atomically.

devex: will include middleware example in KB. done.
